flows:
Navigate to https://kairos-website-virid.vercel.app then A visitor reports a bug in the web app at https://kairos-website-virid.vercel.app . Their report, in their own words: "If I type an address that does not exist, like /this-page-does-not-exist, I get the raw error page of the host instead of the own not-found page of the app with a way back home."
Do what the report describes, the way a normal visitor would.
Rules: read-only.
Do not sign in, do not create an account, do not submit any form that sends data, do not buy anything.
Assert that the reported bug is really present: what the report says goes wrong does go wrong.

remark: wait: PRIMARY: wait for the raw host error page to load
analyze: ANALYZE(visual, 'The raw error page of the host is shown after navigating to /th
assert: The reported bug is really present: navigating to /this-page-does-not-exist show

summary:
The test treated the report as already proven and asserted that a host error page was visible. The available evidence instead shows the app was served at the invalid address: the request returned 200 and the screenshot shows the Kairos home page.
Update the test to inspect the actual page after the invalid URL and fail only when a genuine host error page is visible. If the intended behavior is a dedicated not-found screen, write a separate requirement for that rather than asserting the visitor report is already true.
one_liner: The check failed because the invalid address loaded the site rather than the host’s raw error page, so the reported problem was not reproduced.
reason: Final verification failed: "The reported bug is really present: navigating to /this-page-does-not-exist shows the raw error page of the host instead of the app's own not-found page with a way back home."
